shell.title: AI content moderation
shell.subtitle: Sample console for the moderation team of a fictional platform: a risk-ranked queue, decisions with reasons and an audit trail, threshold rules that move the queue, appeals with deadlines and care for the people who moderate.
shell.sampleHint: Platform, users, cases and figures are fictional. What you do is saved only in your browser.
shell.rulesBadge: Rule-based classification · AI only in «Explain with AI»
shell.rulesHint: The queue is classified in your browser with words and patterns, not with an AI model. The «Explain with AI» button does query a model from our server.
shell.resetConfirm: Delete your decisions, rules and records and go back to the sample data?
shell.resetDone: You are back to the sample data.

how.title: How this demo works
real: Each case's classification: a rule-based classifier reads the text (or the sample description or transcript) and computes the category, the confidence and the fragments that explain it.
Threshold rules: you decide what happens based on confidence; the queue shows where each case would go and «Apply rules to the queue» resolves the automatic ones.
Approve, reject (with policy and measure), escalate (to a team) and correct the category: every decision goes to the audit log and changes the figures.
Appeals with a deadline that runs on real time, an audit log you can export to CSV and a sample transparency report in PDF.
Wellbeing: blur by default, a break that hides the queue, a check-in and rotation away from sensitive categories.
«Explain with AI»: an AI model on our server reads the content and the platform policy and cites the section that applies.
sim: The platform, users and cases are fictional; insults, groups and contact details are masked.
For images, video and audio there are no real files: a sample description or transcript is classified.
The transparency report figures and the simulator's batch of 240 items are sample data.
Escalating, warning or suspending notifies no one: it is recorded in the demo.
The integration examples are illustrative: there is no public moderation API.
tour: In «Moderation queue» open the off-platform payment case (c-2041) and look at the highlighted reasons and the policy that applies.
Reject a case choosing a policy and a measure, and find it in «Audit».
In «Rules» activate rule 8 (illegal lending), save and see how the simulator and the route of case c-2043 change.
Press «Apply rules to the queue» so the rules resolve the automatic cases.
In «Classification» paste your own text, send it to the queue and ask «Explain with AI».
how.project: In your project we connect your platform, load your policies, use a moderation model or an LLM with your examples and measure accuracy with your data before committing to figures.

demoModeration.compliance: Compliance: in your project we help you document your platform's policies and comply with Colombia's Law 1581 of 2012 (personal data) and child protection rules. This demo does not certify compliance.

minors.name: Child protection
minors.signals: secrets from parents or teachers, moving to a private chat, meeting alone; reinforced by: mentions of a tutor, student or school, asking for a phone number.

selfHarm.name: Self-harm
selfHarm.signals: «I can't take it anymore», «better not to wake up», «kill myself», «I feel empty».

sexual.name: Sexual content
sexual.signals: nudity, pornography, selling nudes or intimate photos; reinforced by: «explicit».

hate.name: Hate or discrimination
hate.signals: masked group, «plague» or «rats», «shouldn't be allowed to live here», «women/men only»; reinforced by: marital status and age in a job offer.

harassment.name: Harassment or threats
harassment.signals: insults, «I'm going to find you», «I know where you live», «get lost», «I hope they fire him».

scam.name: Scam or fraud
scam.signals: paying for a kit or registration, earnings per day or week, doubling money, guaranteed returns; reinforced by: «from home», «today only», shortened links.

impersonation.name: Impersonation
impersonation.signals: «official help desk», asking for codes or passwords, «unlock your account», usernames like «Support_Official».

illegalLending.name: Illegal lending
illegalLending.signals: loans with no paperwork or instant loans, daily collection; reinforced by: «no credit bureau check», a mobile number.

offPlatform.name: Off-platform payment or contact
offPlatform.signals: mobile numbers, emails, «outside the platform», «text me», avoiding the fee.

fakeReview.name: Fake review
fakeReview.signals: identical reviews, accounts created today, paying for reviews; reinforced by: «5 stars».

spam.name: Spam
spam.signals: repeated words, «!!!», shortened links, «join now», «win prizes», giveaways.

classifier.title: Classification
classifier.subtitle: Try the demo's rule-based classifier with your own text and see how it decides. It is not an AI model.
classifier.tryHint: Type or paste a comment, listing or message (up to 500 characters), or use an example.
classifier.placeholder: For example: I'll sell it cheaper if you pay me outside the app…
classifier.privacy: Classification runs in your browser. Only «Explain with AI» sends the text to our server; don't paste personal data.
classifier.noSignals: No signals of any policy found.
classifier.noRule: No rule matches: it would go to human review.
classifier.sentAuto: {id} arrived and rule {n} resolved it on its own: {action}. See it in Audit.
classifier.howText: It looks for {n} signals (words and patterns in Spanish and English) ignoring accents and capitals. Each signal adds confidence to its category and the category with the most confidence wins; if none reaches 20%, the result is «No violation».
classifier.severityNote: The colored tag is the category's severity: together with confidence, it sets the priority in the queue.

text.demo: The text is classified as is with the rule-based classifier.
text.project: A text moderation model or an LLM with your policies and examples in Colombian Spanish, with your community's slang.

image.demo: There are no real images: a sample description and the text detected in the image are classified. Sensitive images are shown as a blurred placeholder.
image.project: An image analysis service plus reading the text in the image (OCR). The provider is chosen and measured with your data.

video.demo: There are no real videos: a sample transcript is classified.
video.project: Audio transcription and analysis of key frames with the same text and image classifiers.

audio.demo: There are no real audio files: a sample transcript of the voice note is classified.
audio.project: Automatic speech-to-text and then the text classifier.

classifier.noMetricsNote: The demo shows no model accuracy figures: accuracy is measured with your data during the evaluation. In «Metrics» you can see how the rule-based classifier does with the demo's examples.

ai.persona: You are a trust and safety analyst for a sample platform. You receive a reported piece of content. Use only the policy sections that come with the question: say which one applies (or that none applies), explain why in one or two sentences and what action that section indicates. Do not repeat insults or personal data from the content.

rules.unsaved: {n, plural, one {You have # unsaved change} other {You have # unsaved changes}}: the simulator compares with the saved rules, which are the ones the queue uses.
rules.matches: {n, plural, =0 {Matches no items in the sample batch.} one {Matches # item in the sample batch.} other {Matches # items in the sample batch.}}
rules.empty: There are no rules: everything would go to human review.
rules.howApply: Saved rules mark in the queue where each case goes; automatic ones are resolved with «Apply rules to the queue».
rules.simHint: What the rules would do with a sample batch of {n} items from 24 hours.
